thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: gpu-pool-eu-west capacity exhausted, autoscale not responding. alerts: inference_queue_ms > 95thpct, node-gpu-allocatble=0 (5123456789)

alice: i'm the oncall. seeing massive queueing on eu-west inference endpoints. paging for live mitigation.

devin: confirmed. all nodes in gpu-pool-eu-west show gpu.util=100% and pods Pending=120. kube-scheduler can't place pods due to node allocatable GPU count hitting 0.

ben: HPA events show no recent scale up. the custom metrics adapter (custom-metrics-adapter) returning 504 for /apis/external.metrics.k8s.io. suspect adapter backlog/oom.

carla: metrics-adapter logs show high goroutine count and repeated errors: "query timed out" from upstream Prom. adapter memory trending to 2.8Gi and then OOMKilled on restart.

alice: customer impact?

liz: CS report: several paying clusters report 503s and soft timeouts; top-tier accounts X and Y pinged support. Marking severity: Sev2 (degraded core inference).

ben: immediate steps I recommend:
- Put inference endpoints into slow-path: reduce max concurrency per pod to limit tail latency
- Launch a tiny metrics-bridge that polls PromQL for queue_ms and posts to k8s external metric API directly
- Temporarily increase nodepool size by +10 GPUs (hot spare)
- Create emergency HPA that targets the new external metric from metrics-bridge

devin: i can lower concurrency via a quick config patch to the deployment: set ENV MAX_CONCURRENCY=6 and roll. that will reduce saturation per pod while we add capacity.

carla: deploying metrics-bridge (single-replica) with minimal memory. config: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: metrics-bridge-euw
  namespace: monitoring
spec:
  containers:
  - name: bridge
    image: redwood/metrics-bridge:canary
    env:
    - name: PROM_ENDPOINT
      value: "http://prometheus.monitoring.svc:9090"
    - name: QUERY
      value: "avg_over_time(inference_queue_ms{pool=\"eu-west\"}[1m])"
    resources:
      limits:
        memory: "200Mi"
```

ben: creating emergency HPA (external metric) that points to metrics-bridge via the external metrics adapter we control. hpa min 6 max 128 to allow aggressive scaling.

alice: do the nodepool scale too. open cloud console nodepool request and set autoscaling min to current+10 for 30m.

liz: notifying affected customers: "We are scaling capacity and enabling fallback autoscaling; performance should improve in ~15 mins."

ops-bot: job 9021: kubectl apply -f deploy/metrics-bridge/eu-west-fallback.yaml started.

carla: metrics-bridge started and responding at /metrics. adapter now scrapes it and the external metric shows up in k8s as inference_queue_ms_external. HPA reads metric and begins scaling.

ben: main HPA (inference-hpa-eu-west) had maxReplicas=48 which capped the original rollout. created emergency-hpa-euw with maxReplicas=128. patched target to include deployment inference-svc-eu-west.

devin: nodepool +10 request accepted; nodes coming up. once nodes join, scheduler will move pending pods.

alice: any quick mitigation for the adapter root cause?

carla: root cause analysis in logs: a recent relabeling change in Prometheus scrape config exploded timeseries cardinality for metrics with label job=ml-queue, causing the adapter to fetch huge responses. reverting relabel will be next deploy. for now, reducing Prom scrape concurrency and increasing scrape_timeout for non-critical targets helped adapter stability.

ben: rollout plan: revert relabel (PR ready), then redeploy prometheus with reduced cardinality config; after stable, remove emergency-hpa and metrics-bridge. also audit HPA maxReplicas across inference deployments.

alice: handoff: i need to hand off to ben for ~45m. ben take it and keep me posted. i'll draft an incident stub for the postmortem.

ben: taking over. current status: metrics-bridge feeding metric, emergency-hpa scaling up to 96 replicas, nodepool adding 10 GPUs, concurrency reduced. error rate for top accounts down from 18% to 4%.

liz: CS update: customers X,Y,Z notified of mitigation. support ticket numbers attached in INF-9004.

carla: followups created: INF-9005 (revert relabel + adapter GC tuning), INF-9006 (HPA maxReplicas audit), INF-9007 (permanent metrics-bridge runbook). assigned and linked to thread.

devin: note: we should add a low-precision queue metric as a permanent external metric that is cheap to compute and HPA can use as safety net. low cost and less cardinality.

alice: agreed. ben, mark action item to implement low-precision metric and a canary that toggles adapter failures to ensure HPA fallback works.

ben: will do. handoff summary posted to incident channel and INF tickets updated.

incident-bot: Incident 5123456789 acknowledged by alice at 5123456789. status: mitigated->partial recovery. updates will post here.

ben: closing note for handoff: watch for adapter OOMs and HPA event spikes; remove emergency-hpa only when normal HPA sees metric and scales reliably above baseline.

alice: thanks all. i'll put together a timeline tomorrow and start the postmortem draft. reopen thread if regressions.

ben: will upload HPA events, adapter memory graphs, and Prometheus query timings to INF-9005.
